work_completed: All changes are in `src/gov/guard/bash_writes.py`; `decide.py` was not needed.
- **(a) `read`-bound variables.**
  - `_read_bound` collects the variables `read` binds in a text that holds a `<<<`: its non-option words, an `-a` array, or REPLY.
  - The set is shared with every nested judgement.
  - `names_read_var` gives the unresolvable target when one of those variables is a command's name. Covered forms: `$f`, `${f}`, `"$f" x`, `$a $b`, and after `env`, `command`, `time` or `nohup`.
  - It also fires when the variable is an argument of a program that runs its words: `xargs`, `sudo`, `doas`, `parallel`, `watch`, `stdbuf`, `find -exec`.
  - A variable used only as an argument of a non-running command stays free (`echo $f`, `cat "$f"`, `ls $a`).
- **(b) `mapfile`/`readarray -C`.**
  - `Judgement.callback` reads `-C` as a separate word, joined (`-tC`), or glued to its value (`-C'cmd'`).
  - A literal callback is judged as that command through `self.sub`.
  - A callback that is a variable or a substitution gives the unresolvable target.
  - A callback whose command is not one the walker knows gives the unresolvable target. That covers a function such as `cb`. Known commands are the `_NOT_RUNNERS` list, the shells and `python`; `mapfile -C echo` stays free.
  - It applies to `mapfile`/`readarray` with or without a here-string.
- I wrote the unit file first and watched 27 of its 37 cases fail on 98eff3c84 before the fix.
- One paragraph added to the F1 section of `docs/changes/W2-42a-evidence.md`.

tests: every pytest ran through the heavy slot with `HOME=$TMPDIR/empty-home` and `-m "not local_only" -k "not real and not green_here and not time_limit"`. That exclusion leaves out the real-model cases, which the CTO runs outside the sandbox. I started no embedder, reranker or model.

discoveries:
- `lead()` returns `[]` for `stdbuf`, `setsid`, `chrt`, `ionice` and `taskset`, so a command name behind them is invisible to the head check. I handle those as wrappers.
- `tokens()` removes quotes, so `'$f'` as a command name is also flagged. That is a harmless false positive.

risks:
- Fail-closed false positives:
  - `xargs echo $f` and `sudo echo $f` give the unresolvable target, because any use of a read variable in a wrapper's words counts. A first-word-only rule would miss `xargs -n 1 $f`.
  - `mapfile -C <function or unknown program>` is refused, even when the program is harmless.
- Not covered, as decided in the brief: `read f < file; $f` with no here-string, and a variable read inside a substitution but used outside it.
- A `-C` callback is run by bash with the index and line appended. I judge the callback string as written, not with those two extra arguments.

lessons: `_NOT_RUNNERS` is defined after the first helper block in the module, so a module-level constant built from it has to sit below that definition. My first placement raised `NameError` on import.

proposed_decisions: none.

unresolved: two `tests/unit/hooks/test_live_hook.py` cases fail, and they fail the same way on 98eff3c84 when run against the base `bash_writes.py` under the empty `HOME`. They are `test_a_catastrophic_rm_is_refused[outside the project]` and `test_the_reason_is_plain`. Both expect the reason "outside the project" for `rm -f ~/.bashrc` and got an empty reason. They look environmental, caused by the `HOME` override, but I did not confirm that with the real `HOME`.
